newsitem.title: UK: UK opposition names "Mr Clean" election candidate.
newsitem.headline: UK opposition names "Mr Clean" election candidate.

text.p: Britain's two main opposition parties on Sunday named a joint "anti-sleaze" election candidate to fight against a Conservative politician they accuse of taking money to ask parliamentary questions.

Labour and the Liberal Democrats backed veteran BBC television war correspondent Martin Bell to stand as an independent against Neil Hamilton, who denies allegations of corruption, in the May 1 general election.
Bell will replace Labour candidate Jon Kelly and Liberal Democrat Roger Barlow in the Tatton constituency in northwest England unless Hamilton does not stand.
Hamilton, a former industry minister, had a strong majority of 15,860 in the 1992 election, making Tatton the Conservatives' fifth safest seat.

But an opinion poll in Sunday's Observer newspaper suggested that a high-profile anti-corruption candidate agreed by both Labour and the Liberal Democrats could unseat Hamilton if he remained the Conservative candidate.

Bell is one of the BBC's best-known correspondents, who always wears white suit for luck. He has reported on wars for 30 years and recently expressed a desire to become a "peace correspondent" but such a post has not been forthcoming.

Hamilton had been under intense pressure from the Conservative leadership to step down, but party chiefs have now moderated their stance and he is expected to be formally adopted as a candidate by local Conservatives on Tuesday.
